title: Kaysender Main-Line Editor Production Roadmap
purpose: Define the dependency-safe order in which alpha demonstrators are promoted into full campaign-operation editors and the remaining main-line editors are constructed.

policy.rule: Only one main-line editor may be the active implementation target at a time. A later editor may receive schema notes or fixtures, but not a competing runtime implementation before the active editor clears its exit gate.
policy.generatorRelationship: A generator is an accelerator inside or beside an editor. Random output alone does not satisfy editor completion.
requiredSharedActions: Randomize selected fields without overwriting locked fields
Show inherited source records and provenance

productionOrder.title: Shared Editor Kernel and Profile Contract
productionOrder.reason: Every existing editor currently duplicates form, import, export, error, and panel behavior. More importantly, downstream alpha importers expect older flat fields while newer profiles export nested canonical structures. The shared kernel must normalize profiles before editor-specific expansion continues.
requiredInputs: existing island, settlement, airship, crafting, NPC, and wiki schemas
requiredOutputs: stable profile ID and schema version
exitCriteria: All three existing alpha editors can open through the shared shell
Current island profiles import into settlement and airship editors without flat-field assumptions
Malformed or wrong-profile imports produce actionable errors instead of silent failure
Every editor exposes a dedicated New blank record action
Shared behavior is covered by automated validation and smoke tests

productionOrder.title: Promote Floating Island / Skyland Editor
productionOrder.reason: The skyland is the root spatial and resource object consumed by settlements, ecology, routes, markets, factions, crises, and encounters.
exitCriteria: Map cells can be deliberately edited rather than only generated
Every site, resource, and hazard has a stable ID and map reference
Derived acreage, population capacity, water, drift, and fracture outputs validate
Profile imports and exports round-trip without data loss
Settlement, ecology, and route fixtures can consume the exported profile

productionOrder.title: Population and Demographics Editor
productionOrder.reason: Settlement capacity, workforce, militia, specialists, poverty, migration, disease, and later district demand require a reusable population object rather than a single population number.
exitCriteria: Percentages and head counts reconcile exactly
Population can be attached to an island, settlement, district, ship, or organization
NPC and crew generators can consume population-band weights
Settlement fixtures can inherit workforce, demand, and vulnerability data

productionOrder.title: Promote Settlement / Skyport Editor
productionOrder.reason: Settlements transform island capacity and population into governance, infrastructure, production, defense, scarcity, and civic pressure. They are the primary hub object for most campaign activity.
exitCriteria: Settlement limits cannot exceed parent island capacity without explicit warnings
Stocks, production, consumption, and population pressures reconcile
Defense, dock, and civic assets have stable IDs
A settlement can export district slots, market demand, route-node data, and faction opportunities
Round-trip import preserves inherited island and population provenance

productionOrder.title: City District, Civic Site, and Facility Editor
productionOrder.reason: Large settlements need editable internal places before markets, factions, crimes, encounters, and jobs can be anchored to real locations.
requiredOutputs: dock, market, temple, guild, military, industrial, cistern, slum, and residential sites
exitCriteria: District population and footprint reconcile with the parent settlement
Every major civic asset can be assigned to a district or site
Market, faction, NPC, crime, encounter, and job records can reference stable district and site IDs

productionOrder.title: Crafting, Equipment, Ship Module, and Production Editor
productionOrder.reason: The current crafting engine generates recipes and simulations, but full vessel, market, workshop, and organization editors require deliberate recipe editing, production planning, installation compatibility, and inventory handoff.
exitCriteria: Generated projects can be edited without losing template provenance
Items and modules validate against the crafting-project schema
Ship modules expose mass, slot, power, crew, maintenance, and compatibility fields
Markets and organizations can consume production and inventory records
Airship fixtures can install exported modules and cores

productionOrder.title: NPC, Crew, Household, and Roster Editor
productionOrder.reason: Ships, factions, markets, organizations, and missions need persistent people and teams, not disposable random NPC cards.
exitCriteria: Generated NPCs can be promoted into persistent records
Crew requirements can be compared with available qualified personnel
Population, settlement, vessel, faction, and organization records can reference stable NPC and roster IDs

productionOrder.title: Promote Airship / Vessel Editor
productionOrder.reason: A complete vessel must be assembled from quantitative hull, core, module, cargo, crew, maintenance, legal, and capability records before routes and fleet operations can evaluate it.
requiredOutputs: lift, speed, range, maneuver, altitude, and weather envelope
exitCriteria: Mass, payload, slots, power, and crew requirements reconcile
Installed crafting projects retain their source IDs and maintenance data
Damage and repair states affect derived vessel capabilities
Route and organization fixtures can consume the vessel capability envelope
Imported island and settlement context uses canonical adapters

productionOrder.title: Sky Ecology, Creature, Herd, and Disease Editor
productionOrder.reason: Routes, markets, settlements, hazards, encounters, hunting, and conservation all need persistent ecological populations and material yields tied to altitude and terrain.
exitCriteria: Species and herd records can occupy island cells and route segments
Material yields can feed markets and crafting
Disease and migration outputs can affect settlements and encounters
Creature records reference converted stat blocks or clearly marked stat stubs

productionOrder.title: World Region, Route, and Airspace Editor
productionOrder.reason: Routes must connect real island and port nodes, test actual vessel capability envelopes, and include weather, ecology, resupply, and hazard segments before trade or faction territory can be calculated.
exitCriteria: Every route connects stable node IDs
Travel time and supply use can be calculated for imported vessels
Route hazards and closures are segment-specific
Market, faction, piracy, encounter, and job fixtures can reference route and region IDs

productionOrder.title: Market, Supply Chain, Inventory, and Production Editor
productionOrder.reason: Prices and availability should emerge from production, consumption, inventory, route capacity, ship cargo, and scarcity rather than from isolated random stalls.
exitCriteria: Goods can be traced from producer through route and vessel to market inventory
Prices respond to measurable supply, demand, risk, legality, and quality
Settlement stocks and market inventories reconcile
Faction, organization, piracy, crisis, encounter, and job fixtures can consume market records

productionOrder.title: Faction, Guild, Government, and Fleet Editor
productionOrder.reason: Organizations need concrete territory, leaders, personnel, fleets, markets, clients, revenue, and rivals before influence or conflict can be simulated.
exitCriteria: Every claimed asset references a real profile ID
Faction finance and logistics can be derived from holdings and markets
Territorial influence can be attached to route, region, settlement, and district records
Organization operations, piracy, tithe, encounter, and job fixtures can consume the faction profile

productionOrder.title: Organization Operations, Finance, Logistics, and Project Editor
productionOrder.reason: Ongoing campaign organizations require time, finance, staffing, logistics, maintenance, research, reputation, and crisis resolution across turns.
exitCriteria: Every resource change has a recorded cause
Operations cannot assign unavailable people, assets, or inventory
Time advancement updates maintenance, supply, finance, projects, and crises consistently
Black-market, tithe, encounter, and job editors can consume organization state

productionOrder.title: Black Market, Piracy, Smuggling, and Criminal Network Editor
productionOrder.reason: Criminal operations are overlays on legitimate routes, markets, ships, officials, and factions. Building them earlier would create disconnected random crime tables rather than actionable networks.
exitCriteria: Contraband moves through real suppliers, routes, vessels, and markets
Bribed officials and agents reference persistent NPC or faction records
Evidence and heat can escalate into encounters, crises, and jobs

productionOrder.title: Draconic Tithe, Settlement Crisis, and Intervention Editor
productionOrder.reason: A tithe or major civic crisis must consume actual stocks, money, transport, leadership, enforcers, collaborators, and time rather than exist as an isolated prompt.
requiredOutputs: remaining food, water, coin, and labor
exitCriteria: Crisis demands deduct from real ledgers
Countdown transitions have explicit triggers
Intervention choices alter settlement, market, faction, organization, and route state
Encounter and job fixtures can consume the active crisis

productionOrder.title: Encounter, Hazard, Chase, and Conflict Editor
productionOrder.reason: Playable encounters should assemble existing locations, participants, hazards, vehicles, motives, and consequences rather than fabricate disconnected substitutes for those systems.
requiredOutputs: state changes if won, lost, avoided, or ignored
exitCriteria: Every participant and location can reference a persistent record
Difficulty and stakes can be adjusted without rebuilding the scene
Resolution exports explicit changes to campaign records
Jobs can embed one or more encounter profiles

productionOrder.title: Job Board, Mission Packet, and Campaign Hook Editor
productionOrder.reason: The mission editor is the capstone composer. It should draw patrons, locations, travel, cargo, rewards, opposition, clocks, and consequences from completed world-state editors.
exitCriteria: Mission packets reference existing records instead of copying disconnected text
Rewards and expenses reconcile with market and organization ledgers
Completion and failure export explicit world-state changes
The packet is printable, exportable, and playable without consulting raw generator output
